Leibniz Series

The partial sums overshoot and undershoot π4\frac{\pi}{4}4π​ in turn, closing in from both sides. The gap between two neighboring partial sums is exactly the error bound.

π4=1−13+15−17+⋯\frac{\pi}{4}=1-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+\cdots4π​=1−31​+51​−71​+⋯
∣SN−π4∣≤12N+1\left|S_N-\frac{\pi}{4}\right|\le\frac{1}{2N+1}​SN​−4π​​≤2N+11​

Examples & Exercises

Prove the alternating-series error bound ∣SN−π4∣≤12N+1\left|S_N - \frac{\pi}{4}\right| \le \frac{1}{2N+1}​SN​−4π​​≤2N+11​.

∣L−SN∣≤∣SN+1−SN∣=12N+1|L - S_N| \le |S_{N+1} - S_N| = \frac{1}{2N+1}∣L−SN​∣≤∣SN+1​−SN​∣=2N+11​
Show proof
  1. For an alternating series ∑k=0∞(−1)kak\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(-1)^k a_k∑k=0∞​(−1)kak​ with ak↓0a_k \downarrow 0ak​↓0, the partial sums oscillate inward: even ones increase, odd ones decrease, and the limit LLL always lies between two consecutive partial sums.
  2. Hence ∣L−SN∣≤∣SN+1−SN∣=aN+1|L - S_N| \le |S_{N+1} - S_N| = a_{N+1}∣L−SN​∣≤∣SN+1​−SN​∣=aN+1​. For the Leibniz series aN+1=12N+1a_{N+1} = \frac{1}{2N+1}aN+1​=2N+11​, so ∣SN−π4∣≤12N+1\left|S_N - \frac{\pi}{4}\right| \le \frac{1}{2N+1}​SN​−4π​​≤2N+11​.
  3. (Convergence of the series itself follows from the alternating series test, since ak=12k+1↓0a_k = \frac{1}{2k+1} \downarrow 0ak​=2k+11​↓0.)

How many terms are needed for three correct decimal places? Use the error bound.

12N+1<0.0005  ⟺  N≥1000\frac{1}{2N+1} < 0.0005 \iff N \ge 10002N+11​<0.0005⟺N≥1000
Show proof
  1. Three correct decimals (rounding) requires error <0.0005< 0.0005<0.0005.
  2. The error bound gives 12N+1<0.0005\frac{1}{2N+1} < 0.00052N+11​<0.0005, i.e. 2N+1>20002N + 1 > 20002N+1>2000. Since 11999≈0.00050025>0.0005\frac{1}{1999} \approx 0.00050025 > 0.000519991​≈0.00050025>0.0005 at N=999N = 999N=999, we need N≥1000N \ge 1000N≥1000.
  3. So a thousand terms are needed — the notorious slowness of the Leibniz series.
